task.description: Idiom/scope gate on ISS-0420's dependency bump (oidcc 3.8.0->3.9.0, bandit 1.12.4->1.12.5, mix.lock only) after SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS, before TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER. Check scope containment, decision-record consistency, independently confirm compile/format cleanliness, and confirm the handoff chain is well-formed.

result.summary:
1. Scope: `git diff eeea924e..HEAD --stat` shows exactly 5 files changed: mix.lock (4 lines: bandit and oidcc version/hash entries), handoffs/registry.json, and this run's own three handoff files (step-00, step-01, step-02). No lib/, priv/, mix.exs, or web/ drift. `git diff eeea924e..HEAD -- mix.lock` confirms only the bandit and oidcc lines changed -- no transitive dependency version moved. This is a pure lockfile bump; no new abstraction, behaviour, macro, or generic plumbing was introduced -- nothing to flag as scope creep. Idiom questions 1-2 (gen_statem usage, per-instance supervision via Letflow.InstanceSupervisor) are not implicated -- no lib/letflow/ source changed. Question 3 (type-safety gap) is not implicated -- no new transition logic.
2. Decision-record consistency: checked docs/migration/decisions/ for any record governing dependency-version policy or pinning strategy -- none exists (ls shows records for web framework, frontend ownership, mobile stack, humanless pipeline, etc., none about dependency versioning). Nothing in this change contradicts an existing decision record. mix.exs itself is untouched (`git diff eeea924e..HEAD -- mix.exs` empty per SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02, re-confirmed via this run's own stat above showing mix.exs absent from the changed-files list) -- both patched versions already satisfy the existing `~> 1.5` (bandit) and ueberauth_oidcc's own `~> 3.2` (oidcc) constraints, so no constraint change to evaluate against any framework-choice decision.
3. Independently ran, foreground, real output, this session (not copied from ISSUE-FIXER's or SECURITY-REVIEWER's report): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -> 'Compiling 182 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, clean exit. `mix format --check-formatted` -> no output, no diff, exit 0. Toolchain used: Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 via asdf shims, confirmed against .tool-versions ('elixir 1.20.3-otp-29' / 'erlang 29.0.5') -- matches the pin exactly, no toolchain-drift risk (checked per docs/anti-patterns.md's toolchain-mismatch entry; that entry describes a different, unrelated historical incident on a mismatched 1.18.3/OTP-27 environment, not applicable here).
4. Handoff chain well-formedness: read step-00 (ORCH git-setup), step-01 (ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis), step-02 (SECURITY-REVIEWER) in full. All three use the identical top-level key set (handoff_id/run_id/workflow_id/step/from_agent/to_agent/file/created_at/started_at/completed_at/status/priority/context/task/result/rework_count/max_rework), no extra top-level keys in any of them, rework_count=0 and max_rework=3 present and consistent across all three. context blocks consistently carry stage/requirement_ids/issue_ids/artifacts_in/branch_name. from_agent/to_agent chain correctly links ORCH->ISSUE-FIXER(via step-00's context, actual routing is step-01's from ISSUE-FIXER)->SECURITY-REVIEWER->REVIEWER(this step), each step's `to_agent` matching the next step's `from_agent`. No malformed JSON, no schema drift.

No BLOCKER, no scope-creep, no idiom violation, no decision-record conflict. This is as clean a case as this gate sees: a mechanical lockfile-only security bump with zero source changes to review for OTP idiom or supervision integrity. Routing to TEST-RUNNER for a final full-suite confirmation before merge (ISSUE-FIXER's full `mix test` attempt timed out at 580s for reasons unrelated to failures -- a real full-suite run, not just the scoped auth/HTTP subset both prior agents already reproduced twice, is still owed before this merges).
